brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) joined by a joint bolt, each with a keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) on slot 2, so both hangers face the same way for mounting on screws in a wall. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors.

Four hook plates (hex-acc-hook, two hooks each) on the opposite side of the cells from the keyhole hangers: slots 1 and 5 on the origin cell, slots 4 and 5 on the east cell. That is up to 8 hooks. The hook plates are the catalog's generic hooks; I did not verify their sizing for specific tools, and I did not add bins or other storage. Hanging load was not assessed.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell wall rack: two hex bases joined with a joint bolt, two keyhole hangers on the wall side, and four hook plates on the front side. check_build is clear (meshClash clear, no errors); only info notes about open cap faces remain, which are optional. Hook spacing and tool fit, and the wall loading, were not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
